about: Signature behaviours, wave 1 (AnimalDex docs/ark/behaviours-plan.md, decision 369): species whose own text states a behaviour an existing recipe shows, but whose recipes lacked it. Each row keeps the stored field and the exact sentence. Applied to src/ark-scene/recipes.json by scripts/ark-signature-recipes.mts (run it after scripts/ark-behaviour-recipes.mts regenerates the table).

additions.name: African Penguin
additions.behaviour: nests in burrows
additions.quote: The burrow-nesting coastal penguin.

additions.name: Aldabra Giant Tortoise
additions.behaviour: female lays eggs in soil nest and leaves
additions.quote: Females lay eggs in soil nests

additions.name: Aldabra Giant Tortoise
additions.behaviour: rests in shade and wallows in heat
additions.quote: Day-active but rests during heat, using shade, wallows, and slow rhythms

additions.name: Alligator Snapping Turtle
additions.behaviour: females leave water to bury clutches
additions.quote: Females leave water to bury clutches in sandy or loose soil

additions.name: Amazon Sailfin Catfish
additions.behaviour: male digs a metre-long tunnel into the riverbank and guards the clutch inside
additions.quote: The male digs and holds the bank tunnel, and the female lays inside it; he guards the clutch until it hatches.

additions.name: Amboina Sailfin Lizard
additions.behaviour: female buries eggs in bank nest
additions.quote: Females dig a shallow nest in soil or sand on the bank above the waterline and bury their eggs.

additions.name: American Badger
additions.behaviour: hunts alongside a coyote
additions.quote: They sometimes hunt near coyotes, each using different strengths

additions.name: American Badger
additions.behaviour: digs rapidly after burrowing prey
additions.quote: American Badgers can dig rapidly after burrowing prey

additions.name: American Crow
additions.behaviour: gathers at communal roosts at dusk
additions.quote: then gather at communal roosts

additions.name: American Kestrel
additions.behaviour: drops from a wire, catches a grasshopper and eats it back on the perch
additions.quote: A kestrel sitting on a roadside wire drops to the verge and flies back with a grasshopper gripped in one foot, then eats it on the perch.

additions.name: American Robin
additions.behaviour: huge communal winter roosts in dense trees
additions.quote: Outside the breeding season birds gather at dusk in communal roosts in dense trees, some holding many thousands.

additions.name: Annam Pond Turtle
additions.behaviour: female digs nest hole
additions.quote: females lay clutches of about 5 to 8 eggs in a hole dug in soil

additions.name: Asian Forest Tortoise
additions.behaviour: pushes into damp leaf litter or mud for hours on warm days
additions.quote: On warm days it pushes itself into damp leaf litter or soft mud and stays there for hours

additions.name: Asian Glossy Starling
additions.behaviour: thousands gather at dusk communal roosts, often with mynas
additions.quote: At dusk, noisy flocks, sometimes in their thousands, gather in communal roosts in tall city trees, palms, or on buildings, often alongside other species.

additions.name: Asian Honey Bee
additions.behaviour: clusters together in cold winters living on stored honey
additions.quote: In regions with cold winters the bees cluster together and live on stored honey until spring.

additions.name: Asian Hornet
additions.behaviour: hovers in front of a beehive and snatches returning bees out of the air
additions.quote: The Asian Hornet hovers in front of a beehive like a tiny helicopter, snatches returning honeybees out of the air and carries them home to feed its larvae.

additions.name: Asian Small-clawed Otter
additions.behaviour: gropes under stones and mud with forepaws
additions.quote: Much of its food is found by touch, as it gropes under stones and in mud with its sensitive forepaws.

additions.name: Barbary Macaque
additions.behaviour: huddles in cold weather
additions.quote: Day-active, sleeping in trees or cliffs and huddling in cold weather, making warmth something the group builds together.

additions.name: Barn Owl
additions.behaviour: flies silently, ghost-like, then strikes prey hidden under grass or snow
additions.quote: Barn Owls hunt small mammals (like voles) in complete darkness, often striking prey hidden under vegetation or snow.

additions.name: Bengal Tiger
additions.behaviour: patient lone stalk then explosive finish
additions.quote: The Bengal Tiger moves alone with patience, silence, and explosive finish.

additions.name: Black-crested Coquette
additions.behaviour: catches tiny insects in flight
additions.quote: Beyond nectar, Coquettes also catch tiny insects and spiders in flight.

additions.name: Black Swan
additions.behaviour: spends long periods preening
additions.quote: Black Swans spend significant time preening their dark plumage, meticulously maintaining their feathers.

additions.name: Blue Wildebeest
additions.behaviour: grazes alongside plains zebra
additions.quote: It often grazes alongside plains zebra, which crop the taller, coarser grass and expose the short growth beneath.

additions.name: Bluestreak Cleaner Wrasse
additions.behaviour: cleans parasites off visiting client fish at a reef station
additions.quote: A reef fish that earns safety by removing parasites and irritation from larger animals.

additions.name: Bocage's Wall Lizard
additions.behaviour: dash from basking spot to catch insects
additions.quote: or by a quick dash from a basking spot

additions.name: Bolivian Squirrel Monkey
additions.behaviour: sleeps huddled in clusters along branches
additions.quote: At night the troop sleeps in tall trees, huddled in small clusters along the branches.

additions.name: Bolivian Squirrel Monkey
additions.behaviour: rubs urine on hands and feet (scent on branches)
additions.quote: Individuals sometimes rub urine onto their hands and feet, leaving scent on the branches they travel along.

additions.name: Brahminy Kite
additions.behaviour: soars over water scanning, swoops only when it spots food
additions.quote: From their high vantage point, Brahminy Kites scan large areas of water and land for fish, crabs, small animals, and carrion, swooping down only when an opportunity is identified.

additions.name: Brazilian Lava Lizard
additions.behaviour: motionless on rock then dashes out at insect
additions.quote: It sits motionless on speckled rock or sand, its grey-brown mottling blending with the surface, until an insect passes and it dashes out.

additions.name: Brown Shrike
additions.behaviour: watches from open perch and drops onto insects and lizards
additions.quote: The Brown Shrike watches from an open perch, drops onto insects and small lizards

additions.name: Brown-throated Sunbird
additions.behaviour: perches beside a flower and probes nectar
additions.quote: perches beside a flower and pushes its curved bill inside to drink nectar

additions.name: Brown Wood Owl
additions.behaviour: perches silently then swoops down on prey
additions.quote: They often perch silently on a branch, listening and watching intently in low light conditions, before swooping down rapidly and silently to capture unsuspecting prey.

additions.name: Buff-tip Moth
additions.behaviour: caterpillars feed together, then separate as they grow
additions.quote: The caterpillars feed together, then separate as they grow

additions.name: Campbell's Dwarf Hamster
additions.behaviour: marks the ground by rubbing its belly
additions.quote: Both sexes carry a scent gland on the belly and mark the ground by rubbing it.

additions.name: Capybara
additions.behaviour: group rests together at the water's edge
additions.quote: often resting communally during the hottest parts of the day or night, frequently partly submerged or at the water's edge

additions.name: Carolina Wolf Spider
additions.behaviour: chases ground insects, pins them with front legs
additions.quote: At night it leaves its burrow and chases down crickets, beetles and other ground insects, pinning them with its front legs before it bites.

additions.name: Carpenter Ant
additions.behaviour: neighbouring majors settle borders with long ritualised front-leg boxing
additions.quote: Neighbouring majors settle borders with long ritualised front-leg boxing rather than constant lethal fights.

additions.name: Carpenter Ant
additions.behaviour: winged males and queens leave in nuptial flights about every 188 days
additions.quote: Nuptial flights follow a circa-semiannual rhythm near one hundred eighty-eight days apart.

additions.name: Chilean Swallow
additions.behaviour: autumn/winter flocks mixing with other swallows
additions.quote: In autumn and winter it gathers in flocks that may mix with other swallow species.

additions.name: Citrus Flatid Planthopper
additions.behaviour: nymphs feed in groups on stems; adults jump or fly off when disturbed
additions.quote: Nymphs hatch in late spring and pass through five stages, often feeding in groups

additions.name: Collared Peccary
additions.behaviour: herd huddles pressed together on cold nights
additions.quote: On cold nights herd members rest pressed tightly together in a cave, under a bank or in thick brush, sharing body heat.

additions.name: Common Bed Bug
additions.behaviour: clusters in cracks and crevices by day
additions.quote: By day it clusters in cracks, seams and crevices near beds.

additions.name: Common Grass Blue
additions.behaviour: roosts on grass stems with wings closed, several close together
additions.quote: In dull weather and overnight it roosts on grass stems or seed heads with the wings closed, often several close together.

additions.name: Common Green Magpie
additions.behaviour: joins mixed-species foraging flocks
additions.quote: is reported to join mixed-species foraging flocks at times.

additions.name: Common House Gecko
additions.behaviour: males fight over feeding spots
additions.quote: they are the ones that call and fight over feeding spots

additions.name: Common House Gecko
additions.behaviour: hunts insects at lit walls at night
additions.quote: Common House Geckos frequently hunt insects attracted to artificial lights on walls and ceilings of human dwellings at night.

additions.name: Common Kestrel
additions.behaviour: hunts from perches more in winter
additions.quote: In winter, when food is short, kestrels hunt more from perches, which costs much less energy than hovering.

additions.name: Common Kingfisher
additions.behaviour: digs a nest tunnel into a riverbank
additions.quote: Common Kingfishers often nest in tunnels dug into riverbanks.

additions.name: Common Marmoset
additions.behaviour: sleeps huddled in vine tangle
additions.quote: The group sleeps huddled together in a vine tangle, dense tree crown or hollow, and rests again in the heat of midday.

additions.name: Common Myna
additions.behaviour: large noisy communal evening roosts
additions.quote: In the evening birds gather in large, noisy communal roosts in trees, sometimes hundreds or thousands together

additions.name: Common Myna
additions.behaviour: follows grazing cattle and ploughs, snapping flushed insects
additions.quote: Mynas follow grazing cattle and ploughs, snapping up grasshoppers and other insects disturbed from the grass.

additions.name: Common Raven
additions.behaviour: follows wolves to carcasses
additions.quote: Ravens follow wolves and other predators to carcasses

additions.name: Common Wall Gecko
additions.behaviour: waits motionless beside wall lamps for moths
additions.quote: On warm nights it stations itself beside outdoor lamps on house walls, clinging motionless until a moth lands within reach.

additions.name: Coppery Titi Monkey
additions.behaviour: family sleeps huddled on a branch
additions.quote: At night the family sleeps huddled together on a branch hidden among dense vines or leaves.

additions.name: Coypu
additions.behaviour: burrows into riverbanks
additions.quote: its burrowing collapses the riverbanks it digs into

additions.name: Crested Serpent Eagle
additions.behaviour: watches the forest floor from a shaded perch below the canopy, drops on snakes and grips behind the head
additions.quote: The eagle hunts from a shaded perch below the canopy, watching the forest floor for movement, rather than quartering the ground in flight.

additions.name: Crimson Sunbird
additions.behaviour: pierces base of tubular flowers to reach nectar
additions.quote: it sometimes pierces the base of long tubular flowers to reach the nectar.

additions.name: Danube River Snail
additions.behaviour: inactive in winter, sheltering in bottom mud
additions.quote: becomes largely inactive in winter, sheltering in bottom mud

additions.name: Desert Cottontail
additions.behaviour: fur-lined nest for young
additions.quote: females give birth to usually 2 to 4 blind, naked young in a fur-lined nest

additions.name: Desert Locust
additions.behaviour: swarms roost in trees, bask in early sun and take off once warm
additions.quote: They roost overnight in trees and bushes, bask in the early sun and take off once warm, usually a few hours after sunrise, settling again before dusk.

additions.name: Diamondback Terrapin
additions.behaviour: females come ashore to dig nests above high-tide line
additions.quote: Females come ashore in early summer to dig nests in sand above the high-tide line

additions.name: Domestic Cat
additions.behaviour: kittens play
additions.quote: Females can bear litters of kittens that learn through play, nursing, and observation.

additions.name: Domestic Dog
additions.behaviour: pups learn through play
additions.quote: Females bear litters and pups develop through play, nursing, and social learning.

additions.name: Domestic Pig
additions.behaviour: group sleeps lying close together
additions.quote: sleeping through the night in groups lying close together

additions.name: Domestic Sheep
additions.behaviour: huddles into a tight mass in cold or threat
additions.quote: In cold weather or when feeling threatened, sheep will huddle closely together, often forming a tight mass.

additions.name: Dusky Sleeper
additions.behaviour: lies still under roots and stones by day, partly covered by sediment
additions.quote: By day it rests motionless on the bottom, tucked under roots, rocks or debris, sometimes partly covered by soft sediment.

additions.name: Eastern Chipmunk
additions.behaviour: carries soil away so the burrow has no spoil heap
additions.quote: Burrow entrances have no spoil heap, because soil is carried away and scattered before the hole is opened.

additions.name: Eastern Gray Squirrel
additions.behaviour: builds dreys of twigs and leaves in high forks
additions.quote: A drey is a ball of twigs and leaves wedged in a high fork and lined with shredded bark or grass, and one squirrel may use several.

additions.name: Eastern Lubber Grasshopper
additions.behaviour: slow clumsy walk; rests at night in small groups on stems
additions.quote: At night and in bad weather it rests clinging to stems and leaves of low vegetation, often in small groups.

additions.name: Emu
additions.behaviour: male sits on the eggs for about eight weeks, scarcely eating, then guards striped chicks
additions.quote: The male incubates the clutch for around eight weeks, eating and drinking very little and losing a large proportion of his body weight, then raises the chicks for over a year.

additions.name: Eurasian Eagle-Owl
additions.behaviour: silent approach and powerful talon strike at night
additions.quote: The owl flies silently, approaching prey undetected, and strikes with powerful talons for a swift, conclusive capture.

additions.name: Eurasian Magpie
additions.behaviour: winter shared roosts of dozens to hundreds
additions.quote: in winter many birds gather at shared roosts that can hold dozens or even hundreds.

additions.name: Eurasian Tree Sparrow
additions.behaviour: flocks roost together at dusk in hedges or reedbeds
additions.quote: Outside the breeding season flocks gather at dusk in dense hedges, ivy or reedbeds to roost together

additions.name: European Hornet
additions.behaviour: hunts on into the night when other wasps have stopped
additions.quote: The European Hornet hunts on into the night, drawn to lit windows, when other wasps have long stopped.

additions.name: European Pond Terrapin
additions.behaviour: digs nest with hind feet, covers and leaves
additions.quote: in a hole dug with the hind feet and then covered and left

additions.name: European Starling
additions.behaviour: shared roosts outside breeding season
additions.quote: outside the breeding season birds gather in shared roosts in reedbeds, conifers, city buildings or under piers and bridges

additions.name: Fowler's Toad
additions.behaviour: shuffles backwards into sand until only its back shows
additions.quote: Fowler's Toad shuffles backwards into loose sand until only its speckled back shows, and that skin looks just like the ground around it.

additions.name: Galápagos Tortoise
additions.behaviour: sleeps half-submerged in mud wallows
additions.quote: At night it sleeps in shallow scrapes, under bushes, or half-submerged in mud wallows and pools.

additions.name: Giant Day Gecko
additions.behaviour: males defend trunk and fight intruders
additions.quote: Males defend a trunk or patch of wall against other males and may fight an intruder that stays.

additions.name: Giant Moray
additions.behaviour: hunts together with groupers
additions.quote: Some morays cooperate with other predators such as groupers in reef hunting systems.

additions.name: Giant Mud Crab
additions.behaviour: digs burrow in mangrove mud, walks out to feed on night high tide
additions.quote: A Giant Mud Crab digs a burrow in soft mangrove mud and hides there by day, then walks out to feed when the tide covers the mud at night.

additions.name: Giant Whip Scorpion
additions.behaviour: digs its burrow with its pincers
additions.quote: It spends the day in a burrow it digs with its pincers

additions.name: Goffin's Cockatoo
additions.behaviour: bites a splinter, trims it and uses it to work seed out of a fruit stone
additions.quote: Some Goffin's cockatoos bite a splinter from a branch, trim it to length and use it to work the seed out of a fruit stone.

additions.name: Golden Stag Beetle
additions.behaviour: males wrestle with antler-like jaws
additions.quote: Antler-like jaws and wrestling

additions.name: Gray Angelfish
additions.behaviour: juveniles run cleaning stations, picking parasites from bigger fish
additions.quote: Juveniles set up cleaning stations and pick parasites from larger fish.

additions.name: Gray Angelfish
additions.behaviour: adult pairs patrol the reef together patch to patch
additions.quote: Adult pairs patrol a wide stretch of reef and hard bottom together, moving steadily from one feeding patch to the next.

additions.name: Great Crow
additions.behaviour: roosts communally in large dry-season aggregations
additions.quote: The species roosts communally in the dry season, sometimes in large aggregations in sheltered gullies.

additions.name: Great Kiskadee
additions.behaviour: brief flights from an exposed perch to prey and straight back, incl. fish off the surface
additions.quote: Attacks are brief outward flights from the perch to the prey and straight back, rather than sustained pursuit or patrolling.

additions.name: Great-tailed Grackle
additions.behaviour: thousands-strong noisy communal roosts
additions.quote: At dusk flocks gather in noisy communal roosts, sometimes thousands strong in winter

additions.name: Greater Kudu
additions.behaviour: males use spiral horns in display and contests
additions.quote: Huge spiral horns in males used for display and contests.

additions.name: Greater Rhea
additions.behaviour: several females lay in one male's scrape; he alone incubates the pooled clutch
additions.quote: Several females lay their eggs into the same scrape made by a single male, producing clutches that can hold twenty to fifty eggs from different mothers.

additions.name: Green Iguana
additions.behaviour: females move to nesting ground and dig burrows
additions.quote: Females lay clutches of eggs in burrows or nest chambers, often after moving to suitable nesting ground.

additions.name: Groundhog
additions.behaviour: young leave to dig their own burrows by midsummer
additions.quote: leave to dig their own burrows by midsummer

additions.name: Guinea Pig
additions.behaviour: huddles together when resting or insecure
additions.quote: Guinea pigs are highly social and often huddle together, especially when resting or feeling insecure.

additions.name: Guppy
additions.behaviour: males display colours and fins to females with special swimming and posturing
additions.quote: Male guppies actively display their vibrant colors and elaborate fins to females through specific swimming patterns and posturing.

additions.name: Hawksbill Sea Turtle
additions.behaviour: probes beak into coral crevices for sponges
additions.quote: The Hawksbill Sea Turtle uses a narrow hooked beak to reach food tucked deep inside coral reefs.

additions.name: House Sparrow
additions.behaviour: noisy flocks gather and chatter before roosting
additions.quote: Before dusk, noisy flocks gather in dense hedges, ivy, creepers or under eaves and chatter loudly before settling for the night.

additions.name: House Wren
additions.behaviour: male starts several dummy nests
additions.quote: males often starting multiple dummy nests nearby

additions.name: Humboldt Penguin
additions.behaviour: digs nest burrows into guano
additions.quote: It is listed as Vulnerable; past guano harvesting destroyed many of the deposits it once dug burrows into.

additions.name: Indian Pied Myna
additions.behaviour: large communal roosts
additions.quote: Indian Pied Mynas gather in large, often noisy, communal roosts

additions.name: Indochinese Tiger
additions.behaviour: silent stalk then short powerful attack
additions.quote: After a silent stalk, the tiger waits for the opportune moment, then launches a sudden, powerful, short-distance attack.

additions.name: Indonesian Blue-tongued Skink
additions.behaviour: forages through leaf litter; shelters in midday heat
additions.quote: It basks in the morning to warm up, then forages through leaf litter, and shelters at night and in the hottest hours under logs, in burrows or in deep litter.

additions.name: Jackdaw
additions.behaviour: communal roosts and flock foraging
additions.quote: Jackdaws roost communally in large numbers and forage in flocks

additions.name: Japanese Beetle
additions.behaviour: clusters on sunlit leaves to feed and mate
additions.quote: clustering on sunlit leaves

additions.name: Javan Ferret-Badger
additions.behaviour: snuffles leaf litter and digs out worms with long claws at night
additions.quote: The Javan Ferret-Badger comes out at night on the forest floors of Java and Bali, snuffling through the leaf litter and digging out worms and insects with its long claws.

additions.name: Javan Myna
additions.behaviour: gathers at roosts before dusk calling until dark
additions.quote: Before dusk birds gather in shared roosts in the dense crowns of roadside trees or on building ledges, calling loudly until dark

additions.name: Komodo Dragon
additions.behaviour: lays eggs in burrows or mound nests
additions.quote: Females lay eggs in nesting burrows or mound nests

additions.name: Kuhl's Pipistrelle Bat
additions.behaviour: females form nursery colonies
additions.quote: Females gather in nursery colonies, usually of 20 to 100 bats, in buildings.

additions.name: Laughing Kookaburra
additions.behaviour: perches still on a branch then swoops to pounce on ground prey
additions.quote: Perch-and-Pounce Hunting: stillness on a branch becomes sudden ground action.

additions.name: Leaf-eating Slug
additions.behaviour: burrows into moist soil by day; dry spells keep it underground
additions.quote: By day it burrows a short way into moist soil or lies flattened beneath stones, and dry spells keep it underground.

additions.name: Leopard Gecko
additions.behaviour: waits at burrow mouths for insects
additions.quote: making it a ground hunter that waits at burrow mouths for passing insects

additions.name: Leopard Tortoise
additions.behaviour: female digs nest
additions.quote: Females dig nests and lay clutches of eggs in soil

additions.name: Leopoldi Stingray
additions.behaviour: lies still by day with sediment flicked over its back
additions.quote: By day it lies still on the river bed for long periods, often with a thin layer of sediment flicked over its back

additions.name: Lesser Banded Hornet
additions.behaviour: hunts honey bees at hive entrances
additions.quote: Colonies hunt honey bees at hive entrances

additions.name: Limpkin
additions.behaviour: slides its bill into an apple snail's shell and snips it free
additions.quote: The Limpkin has a long bill that bends slightly to the right at the tip, a perfect fit for sliding into the curled shell of an apple snail and snipping the snail free.

additions.name: Little Owl
additions.behaviour: sits at its hole entrance sunning by day
additions.quote: Rests by day in a tree hole, barn or rock cleft, often sitting at the entrance in the sun.

additions.name: Little Owl
additions.behaviour: watches from a fence post at twilight, glides down onto voles and beetles
additions.quote: From a fence post at twilight it watches the grass below, then glides down onto a vole or beetle it has picked out by sight and sound.

additions.name: Long-tailed Macaque
additions.behaviour: huddles at branch ends in sleeping trees over rivers
additions.quote: Sleeping trees, often ones overhanging a river, are occupied before dusk, and the animals huddle in small groups near the ends of branches until first light.

additions.name: Long-tailed Macaque
additions.behaviour: uses stones as hammers to open oysters and nuts
additions.quote: On coasts and islands in Thailand and Myanmar, some populations use stones as hammers to open oysters, sea snails and nuts.

additions.name: Malachite Butterfly
additions.behaviour: hangs under leaves at night, sometimes several together
additions.quote: At night adults hang under the leaves of low shrubs, sometimes several together.

additions.name: Malaysian Field Rat
additions.behaviour: nests of shredded vegetation in palm crowns or undergrowth
additions.quote: It spends the day in nests of shredded vegetation hidden in dense undergrowth, frond piles or palm crowns

additions.name: Mandrill
additions.behaviour: males rub chest scent gland on tree trunks
additions.quote: Adult males rub a scent gland on the chest against tree trunks, leaving marks that other mandrills sniff.

additions.name: Mangrove Crab
additions.behaviour: defends burrow entrance with raised claws and sideways shoves
additions.quote: Individuals frequently occupy and maintain the same burrow for long periods, defending the entrance against similar-sized neighbours with raised claws and sideways shoves.

additions.name: Mangrove Horseshoe Crab
additions.behaviour: ploughs through soft mud on the flood, buries on the ebb
additions.quote: Mangrove Horseshoe Crabs move with the tide rather than the clock, ploughing across flats on the flood and burying on the ebb.

additions.name: Masked Lovebird
additions.behaviour: pairs preen each other
additions.quote: Pairs stay together for long periods and preen each other, behaviour that gave lovebirds their common name.

additions.name: Mediterranean House Gecko
additions.behaviour: waits by lamps at night to snap moths
additions.quote: On warm nights it waits beside outdoor lamps and darts out to snap up moths and other insects that the light draws in.

additions.name: Meerkat
additions.behaviour: warms up near burrow in the morning
additions.quote: Meerkats are diurnal, warming up near burrows before foraging and returning underground to rest.

additions.name: Moon Jellyfish
additions.behaviour: gathers in dense swarms near the surface
additions.quote: Often gathers in dense swarms near the surface

additions.name: Mourning Cloak
additions.behaviour: basks with wings spread toward the sun on cold spring mornings
additions.quote: On a cold spring morning it settles with wings spread towards the sun, often on a pale trunk or path, warming its flight muscles before it takes off.

additions.name: Mugger Crocodile
additions.behaviour: digs nest hole in sandy bank
additions.quote: In the dry season the female digs a nest hole in a sandy bank

additions.name: Multicolored Asian Lady Beetle
additions.behaviour: adults gather in large numbers on pale sunlit walls in autumn
additions.quote: In autumn adults gather in large numbers on pale, sunlit walls, then overwinter in cracks, roof spaces and houses.

additions.name: Northern Flicker
additions.behaviour: woodpecker that feeds on the ground, licking up ants
additions.quote: Unlike many woodpeckers, it often feeds on the ground

additions.name: Olive-backed Sunbird
additions.behaviour: flicks constantly between flowers probing nectar
additions.quote: Constant flicking movement between flowers

additions.name: Oriental Garden Lizard
additions.behaviour: hunts from a perch with short rapid attack
additions.quote: The lizard commonly hunts visually from a perch, observing its surroundings before making a short, rapid attack on prey.

additions.name: Oriental White-eye
additions.behaviour: flock mates preen each other
additions.quote: Flock mates often preen each other

additions.name: Osprey
additions.behaviour: plunges feet-first into water to seize fish
additions.quote: The bird plunges feet-first, closes its nostrils on entry, and has dense oily plumage that prevents waterlogging, unlike cormorants which must dry out.

additions.name: Ostrich
additions.behaviour: communal nest around a dominant pair
additions.quote: Females lay large eggs in ground nests, often with communal nesting around a dominant pair.

additions.name: Painted Turtle
additions.behaviour: female digs flask nest in sunny soil near water
additions.quote: females dig a flask-shaped nest in open, sunny soil, usually within about 200 metres of water

additions.name: Palm Cockatoo
additions.behaviour: builds a platform of splintered sticks inside the hollow
additions.quote: Before laying, the pair builds a deep platform of splintered sticks inside the hollow, which may keep the egg above standing water.

additions.name: Pantropical Jumping Spider
additions.behaviour: male jerky side-to-side dance with front legs raised
additions.quote: Males are reported to court females with a jerky side-to-side dance, holding up their front legs.

additions.name: Pantropical Jumping Spider
additions.behaviour: walks into range on a sunny wall, then jumps
additions.quote: The Pantropical Jumping Spider walks into range on a wall, then jumps.

additions.name: Peach-faced Lovebird
additions.behaviour: pairs preen each other
additions.quote: Pairs preen each other and stay together for long periods, which gave lovebirds their common name.

additions.name: Peters's Jumping Spider
additions.behaviour: male dance: waving dark front legs, stepping side to side
additions.quote: Males court females with a dance, raising and waving their dark front legs while stepping from side to side in front of her.

additions.name: Peters's Jumping Spider
additions.behaviour: leaps with silk safety line; a miss ends dangling
additions.quote: Before leaping it attaches a silk safety line to the surface, so a missed jump ends dangling rather than falling.

additions.name: Philippine Crocodile
additions.behaviour: female guards nest near water
additions.quote: Females lay eggs in nests near water and may guard nesting areas.

additions.name: Pied Butcherbird
additions.behaviour: watches from exposed perch, launches at prey, returns to lookout
additions.quote: It watches from an exposed perch, launches when prey reveals itself and returns to a useful lookout.

additions.name: Pied Crow
additions.behaviour: hundreds share dusk roosts in tall trees
additions.quote: Outside the breeding season birds gather towards dusk at shared roosts in tall trees, where hundreds may spend the night together.

additions.name: Plains Zebra
additions.behaviour: stallions fight using canines
additions.quote: have larger canine teeth, which they use in fights

additions.name: Plains Zebra
additions.behaviour: moves ahead of wildebeest, cropping tall grass
additions.quote: On the Serengeti plains, zebras often move ahead of the wildebeest, cropping the tall, coarse grass and exposing shorter growth beneath.

additions.name: Platypus
additions.behaviour: lays eggs in a nesting burrow
additions.quote: Females lay eggs in nesting burrows, a rare trait among mammals.

additions.name: Platypus
additions.behaviour: lays eggs in a nesting burrow
additions.quote: Females lay eggs in nesting burrows, a rare trait among mammals.

additions.name: Racket-tailed Roller
additions.behaviour: watches from a perch then drops to seize prey on the ground
additions.quote: The Racket-tailed Roller watches from a perch, often within the canopy, before dropping to the ground to seize its prey.

additions.name: Rainbow Crab
additions.behaviour: drags food into its burrow
additions.quote: Food is gathered near the burrow, and some is reportedly dragged inside.

additions.name: Red Imported Fire Ant
additions.behaviour: winged queens and males pour from the mound after rain to mate in the air
additions.quote: After rain on warm days, winged queens and males pour from the mound to mate in the air

additions.name: Red River Hog
additions.behaviour: piglets born in sheltered nests
additions.quote: Females give birth to piglets in sheltered nests or dense cover

additions.name: Red Squirrel
additions.behaviour: raises young in dreys
additions.quote: Females raise young in tree nests called dreys

additions.name: Red Tegu
additions.behaviour: female lines nest with plants and guards it
additions.quote: She is reported to line the nest with plant material and to stay and guard it

additions.name: Red Tegu
additions.behaviour: tongue-flicking forager that stops to dig for eggs and grubs
additions.quote: A foraging tegu covers ground steadily, flicking its long forked tongue to pick up scent and stopping to dig where it finds eggs, grubs or fallen fruit.

additions.name: Red-winged Blackbird
additions.behaviour: winter dusk roosts shared with grackles, cowbirds, starlings
additions.quote: Outside the breeding season it gathers at dusk in communal roosts in marshes and thickets, often shared with grackles, cowbirds and starlings

additions.name: Redclaw Crayfish
additions.behaviour: digs shallow burrows into banks
additions.quote: Redclaw crayfish dig shallow burrows into banks and utilize existing submerged cover like logs and rocks.

additions.name: Reticulated River Stingray
additions.behaviour: rests buried to the eyes in sand or mud by day
additions.quote: buried to the eyes in sand or mud

additions.name: Rhinoceros
additions.behaviour: wallows in mud or dust
additions.quote: frequently wallow in mud or dust

additions.name: Rhinoceros Iguana
additions.behaviour: female digs nest
additions.quote: Females dig nests and lay eggs in soil or sand

additions.name: Rice Grasshopper
additions.behaviour: nymphs and adults rest in groups on sunny leaf blades
additions.quote: Nymphs and adults often rest in groups on leaf blades in sunny paddies.

additions.name: Ring-billed Gull
additions.behaviour: gathers over swarms of emerging mayflies and flying ants to hawk them
additions.quote: It catches insects in flight, and gathers over swarms of emerging mayflies and flying ants.

additions.name: Ring-tailed Lemur
additions.behaviour: huddles to sleep in groups
additions.quote: Day-active, sleeping in groups and warming after cool nights, so shared heat becomes a daily ritual rather than just comfort.

additions.name: Roadside Hawk
additions.behaviour: drops from a low post onto prey and flies back up to wait
additions.quote: From a low post it watches the grass below, drops onto a grasshopper, lizard or mouse, and flies back up to wait again.

additions.name: Rook
additions.behaviour: communal roost after feeding
additions.quote: Rooks are diurnal and often gather to roost communally after feeding.

additions.name: Russian Tortoise
additions.behaviour: digs metre-long burrows with strong forelimbs
additions.quote: Its compact body and strong forelimbs are built for digging burrows, which are reported to reach a metre or more.

additions.name: Savannah Monitor
additions.behaviour: digs/enlarges burrows and termite mounds, stays in through heat and dry season
additions.quote: It digs its own burrows or enlarges existing holes and termite mounds, then stays inside through the hottest hours and much of the dry season.

additions.name: Scarlet Ibis
additions.behaviour: probes mud with a side-to-side bill sweep
additions.quote: Scarlet Ibises use their long, decurved bills to probe soft mud and shallow water, often with a side-to-side motion, to locate hidden prey like crabs, shrimp, and worms.

additions.name: Siamese Crocodile
additions.behaviour: female guards nest
additions.quote: Females build nests and lay clutches of eggs, often guarding the nest or young.

additions.name: Slender Skimmer
additions.behaviour: catches small insects in mid-air and also other dragonflies
additions.quote: Adults hunt small flying insects on the wing and are also reported to catch and eat other dragonflies.

additions.name: Song Thrush
additions.behaviour: smashes snails against a rock anvil
additions.quote: Song Thrushes repeatedly pick up snails and smash them against a hard surface, typically a specific rock, until the shell breaks.

additions.name: Southeastern Five-lined Skink
additions.behaviour: female coils around her clutch until it hatches
additions.quote: the female usually stays coiled around the clutch until it hatches

additions.name: Southern Cassowary
additions.behaviour: male alone incubates the green eggs and raises the chicks
additions.quote: The male Southern Cassowary takes sole responsibility for incubating the strikingly green eggs and raising the chicks for up to nine months.

additions.name: Southern Mole Cricket
additions.behaviour: digs with shovel-like front legs
additions.quote: The Southern Mole Cricket digs with front legs shaped like little shovels

additions.name: Spotted Wood Owl
additions.behaviour: perches motionless listening most of the night, then a short silent descent
additions.quote: The attack is a short, direct descent from the perch, with strong talons taking the prey at the end, and the owl returns to a perch rather than pursuing a miss.

additions.name: Sri Lankan Elephant
additions.behaviour: dust and mud baths redden the skin
additions.quote: Grey skin, often reddened by dust and mud baths

additions.name: Stalk-eyed Fly
additions.behaviour: gathers at night in aggregations on hanging rootlets over streams
additions.quote: Flies gather at night in aggregations on hanging rootlets and fine vegetation over streams, often dozens together.

additions.name: Stump-tailed Macaque
additions.behaviour: sleeps huddled in contact
additions.quote: At night troop members sleep in tall trees, often sitting huddled together in contact.

additions.name: Sugar Glider
additions.behaviour: group sleeps together in tree hollows
additions.quote: Sugar Gliders sleep in hollows by day and move in social groups through trees at night.

additions.name: Sulcata Tortoise
additions.behaviour: excavates deep burrows and retreats in midday heat/drought
additions.quote: Tortoises are most active during the cooler parts of the day (early morning, late afternoon) and retreat into their burrows during the peak heat of midday or during prolonged dry spells.

additions.name: Sumatran Tiger
additions.behaviour: gets very close undetected then sudden attack
additions.quote: Sumatran Tigers are ambush predators, relying on getting very close to their prey undetected before launching a sudden, powerful attack.

additions.name: Termite
additions.behaviour: winged alates pour out in brief rainy-season swarms
additions.quote: Winged alates emerging in brief rainy-season swarms

additions.name: Threadfin Acara
additions.behaviour: pair digs a breeding tunnel in the river bed and guards its entrance
additions.quote: Parent fish actively patrol and defend the immediate area around the opening of their excavated nest.

additions.name: Tiger Moth
additions.behaviour: blackish yellow-ringed larvae feed in groups under fig leaves
additions.quote: Larvae rest beneath Ficus leaves and feed in groups after eggs are laid in batches.

additions.name: Tokay Gecko
additions.behaviour: may guard eggs stuck to surfaces
additions.quote: Females lay eggs in sheltered places, often attached to surfaces, and may guard them in some situations.

additions.name: Tropical House Gecko
additions.behaviour: waits beside lamps at night to snap insects
additions.quote: The Tropical House Gecko settles on the wall beside a lamp after dark and snaps up the insects that the light draws in.

additions.name: Tufted Capuchin
additions.behaviour: sleeps sitting close together in palm crowns
additions.quote: At dusk the group settles in tall trees, often in palm crowns or large emergent trees, and sleeps on branches with members sitting close together.

additions.name: Tufted Capuchin
additions.behaviour: squirrel monkeys travel alongside
additions.quote: Squirrel monkeys often travel with tufted capuchin groups, following them through the canopy and feeding alongside them.

additions.name: Tufted Capuchin
additions.behaviour: cracks nuts with stones
additions.quote: Tufted Capuchins are known for tool use in some populations, such as using stones to crack nuts.

additions.name: Tufted Gray Langur
additions.behaviour: spotted deer feed below on leaves it drops; both bolt at each other's alarm
additions.quote: The Tufted Gray Langur feeds in the treetops while spotted deer gather below for the leaves it drops, and each species bolts at the other's alarm call.

additions.name: Two-striped Telamonia
additions.behaviour: male courtship: raised waving front legs, sideways steps
additions.quote: males court females with a display of raised, waving front legs and sideways steps

additions.name: Vampire Crab
additions.behaviour: day in burrow dug into damp bank, out from dusk
additions.quote: In the wild they are thought to spend daylight hours in a burrow dug into a damp bank, or under stones, roots and leaf litter, where the air stays humid.

additions.name: Welcome Swallow
additions.behaviour: flocks roost together in reedbeds, wires, ledges
additions.quote: Outside the breeding season birds gather to roost together, sometimes in large flocks

additions.name: Western Gorilla
additions.behaviour: tests swamp depth with a stick before wading
additions.quote: A wild female in the Republic of the Congo was photographed testing the depth of a swamp pool with a stick before wading in.

additions.name: Western Honey Bee
additions.behaviour: overwinters as a shivering cluster
additions.quote: overwinters as a cluster that shivers to keep its centre near 34 degrees Celsius

additions.name: Western Lowland Gorilla
additions.behaviour: young play and stay close
additions.quote: Young gorillas spend years learning social life through play and closeness.

additions.name: Western Yellow Wagtail
additions.behaviour: runs around the feet of grazing cattle catching flushed insects
additions.quote: The Western Yellow Wagtail runs around the feet of grazing cattle and snaps up the insects they stir from the grass.

additions.name: White-nosed Coati
additions.behaviour: digs and sniffs with snout and claws
additions.quote: Claws and nose together: digging and smelling turn curiosity into food.

additions.name: White-throated Kingfisher
additions.behaviour: nests at the end of a long tunnel
additions.quote: Snakes, monitor lizards and rats are the likeliest threats to eggs and chicks, which are protected by the long nest tunnel.

additions.name: White-throated Kingfisher
additions.behaviour: drops from a wire or branch onto lizards, crabs and insects far from water
additions.quote: The White-throated Kingfisher often hunts far from water, dropping from a wire or branch onto lizards, frogs, crabs and large insects as well as fish.

additions.name: Yellow Tang
additions.behaviour: cleans algae off the shells of visiting green sea turtles
additions.quote: It cleans algae off the shells of green sea turtles, which visit reef to be groomed.

additions.name: Yellowfin Surgeonfish
additions.behaviour: feeds in mixed groups with other surgeonfishes over open sand
additions.quote: It is often reported feeding in mixed groups with other surgeonfishes over open ground rather than alone.

additions.name: Zebu
additions.behaviour: herd lies down together at night
additions.quote: At night the herd lies down together

additions.name: Broad-bodied Chaser
additions.behaviour: female hovers and flicks her abdomen tip into the water to lay while the male guards
additions.quote: The female then lays alone, hovering and flicking the tip of her abdomen into the water over submerged plants while the male guards nearby.

additions.name: Common Flangetail
additions.behaviour: female flies low tapping her abdomen tip on open water to release eggs
additions.quote: Females lay eggs by flying low and tapping the abdomen tip on open water, releasing eggs that sink to the bottom.

additions.name: Scarlet Skimmer
additions.behaviour: female taps her abdomen on the water to wash off eggs with the male hovering close
additions.quote: the female flies low over open water and taps the tip of her abdomen on the surface to wash off eggs, often with the male hovering close by

additions.name: Wandering Glider
additions.behaviour: female taps eggs into temporary pools in flight, spreading the clutch across several
additions.quote: Eggs are dropped straight into temporary pools with the female tapping the water surface in flight, spreading a clutch across several pools rather than committing it all to one that might dry.
